title: Elijah Wood Confirms Return as Frodo in The Hunt for Gollum; Details on Stephen Colbert's Shadow of the Past Project
text:
Elijah Wood clarifies his return as Frodo Baggins for The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, set for 2027, while discussing the development status of Stephen Colbert's separate film, The Lord of the Rings: Shadow of the Past, which adapts six omitted chapters from The Fellowship of the Ring.
Elijah Wood , who originally portrayed Frodo Baggins in The Lord of the Rings trilogy and briefly in The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey, is set to reprise the role in an upcoming film titled The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, directed by Andy Serkis and scheduled for release on December 17, 2027.
This new project is part of a broader expansion of the franchise, but it is distinct from another planned film, The Lord of the Rings: Shadow of the Past, which is being developed by Stephen Colbert and his son Peter McGee alongside Philippa Boyens. Wood, in an interview with The Direct, clarified that while he is enthusiastic about the possibility of returning for Shadow of the Past, that film is not yet officially greenlit; the script must be completed and various creative and business steps finalized before moving forward.
In contrast, The Hunt for Gollum is already in active production, marking Wood's confirmed return to the iconic character after more than a decade. The Shadow of the Past adaptation aims to fill narrative gaps from the original 2001 film, The Fellowship of the Ring, by bringing to life six chapters that were omitted to maintain pacing and momentum.
These chapters, spanning from "Three is Company" to "Fog on the Barrow-Downs," follow Frodo's early journey from the Shire to Bree, accompanied by Sam, Pippin, and Merry, and include key elements like the Barrow-wights and Tom Bombadil. Colbert, a lifelong Tolkien enthusiast, is co-writing the script with his son and Boyens, leveraging his deep fandom and the expertise of a seasoned screenwriter.
The project gained clearer footing after the conclusion of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, freeing Colbert to dedicate his attention to this cinematic venture. His cameo as Feldur Hook in The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug underscores his established connection to the franchise.
While Shadow of the Past remains in development, The Hunt for Gollum moves forward with a notable cast: Andy Serkis returns as Gollum, Ian McKellen as Gandalf, with Jamie Dornan as Aragorn, Kate Winslet as Marigold, Leo Woodall as Halvard, Lee Pace as Thranduil, and Anya Taylor-Joy as Seren. The 2027 release will focus on Gollum's story, likely intersecting with Frodo's path.
Meanwhile, the potential for other original hobbit actors-Sean Astin (Sam), Billy Boyd (Pippin), and Dominic Monaghan (Merry)-to rejoin their roles in Shadow of the Past hinges on that project's progression; the four have maintained close friendships and frequently reunite. Additionally, Prime Video's The Rings of Power has touched on Barrow-wights and Tom Bombadil but in a much earlier timeline, ensuring narrative separation from Colbert's film.
Audiences can first anticipate Wood's Frodo in The Hunt for Gollum, with Shadow of the Past offering a deeper dive into the omitted chapters if approved
